# Text

A payment description can carry detail beyond the merchant label, such as
whether the charge is a delivery order. `Text` encodes those free-form strings
with a frozen Hugging Face model. RelFlow learns to combine their representations
with the amount and other fields. It does not fine-tune that encoder or
generate text.

Install the optional text dependency:

```bash
uv add "relflow[text]"
```

```python
import relflow as rf

model = rf.Model.xs(
    amount=rf.Number,
    merchant=rf.Category,
    memo=rf.Text,
    disputed=rf.Boolean(mask=True),
)
```

One labeled payment:

```yaml
amount: 84.50
merchant: North Market
memo: "North Market delivery order"
disputed: false
```

## Input and options

The Arrow leaf must contain strings. An empty string is valued; a null has a
separate state. Tokenization pads and truncates at `max_length`.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `model` | `"google/bert_uncased_L-2_H-128_A-2"` | Hugging Face identifier or local model path. |
| `max_length` | `128` | Positive tokenization length limit. |
| `tokenizer_batch_size` | `4096` | Maximum strings materialized per tokenizer call. |
| `encoder_batch_size` | `32` | Maximum flattened text values per frozen-encoder call. |
| `encoder_pooling` | `"cls"` | `"cls"`, `"mean"`, or `"pooler"`; the last requires `pooler_output`. |
| `cache` | `False` | Reuse pooled frozen-encoder outputs: `True` keeps every distinct input; a positive integer caps retained entries. |
| `objective` | `"l2"` | Embedding reconstruction loss: `"l1"` or `"l2"`. |
| `jitter` | `rf.Jitter()` | Training noise on the pooled frozen embedding before learned projection. |

`cls` and `mean` require `last_hidden_state`. Text fields using the same model
reuse its frozen encoder within the process. Right-padded values are grouped
by length and cropped per encoder batch; left-padded values retain their full
width. `max_length` still controls truncation and tensor storage.

## Repeated text

Repeated descriptions can reuse frozen-encoder outputs across forward passes:

```python
memo = rf.Text(cache=10_000)
```

`cache=False` disables this reuse. `cache=True` retains every distinct tokenized
input encountered; a positive integer retains at most that many entries.
The bounded cache evicts the least frequently reused resident entry, breaking
ties by least recent use. It favors frequent reuse rather than tracking a
global ranking of every description ever seen. Texts that tokenize identically,
including after truncation, can share an entry.

Entries are pristine pooled embeddings stored in CPU memory, separately for
each text field in each process. Encoder device and precision distinguish
entries. Tokenization still runs, as do the trainable projection and training
jitter on every forward pass. Caching therefore preserves their gradients and
fresh noise while avoiding repeated frozen-encoder work.

Checkpoints retain the `cache` setting but omit cached embeddings; a loaded
model starts with an empty cache. Under DDP, each process builds its own cache.
Use a finite cap when inputs contain many distinct descriptions: `cache=True`
has no entry limit and can keep growing in host memory.

## Learning and output

A reconstructing mask trains the decoder against the pristine frozen embedding,
using state loss and the configured content objective on valued targets.
[Jitter](../core-concepts/jitter.qmd) affects only visible continuous inputs,
not strings, token IDs, or target embeddings. Both settings of
`jitter.normalize` act at the same pooled-embedding boundary.

Text has no decoded public state/content payload. `embed=True` exports a
contextual relflow embedding, distinct from the frozen encoder output; see
[shared leaf options](../core-concepts/data-types.qmd#shared-leaf-options).
Use [Vector](vector.qmd) when the source already supplies an embedding.

## External model assets

The first use of a remote model identifier may download tokenizer and encoder
assets. relflow checkpoints save the request and learned relflow weights,
but do not bundle those external assets. Every loading or serving process
must be able to resolve the same identifier or local path. For reproducible
deployment, prepare a pinned encoder directory and ship it with the artifact.
